question: Does the answer depend on the solver path (ANK-only vs ANK+NK)?
mesh: gci_C, 603,592 cells -- COARSE, not gci_M. The historical freeze recorded in solve_s8.py was on gci_M (1,111,152 cells) on 2026-09-11 and was NOT re-run here.

attempt_1.arms: NK enabled on g83/g47/g13 at alpha 0 and 4; plus g83 with ADflow's full preconditioner (NKSubspaceSize 60, NKPCILUFill 2)
attempt_1.result: ALL bit-identical to the ANK-only production runs -- same forces to every printed digit, same iteration counts (286/196/190/159/307/195). Peak 6.9 GiB throughout.
attempt_1.why: All 286 iterations carry IterType = ANK. NKSwitchTol is 1.0e-6 and the L2 stopping target is also 1e-6, so the run terminates before the NK switch can fire.
attempt_1.finding: --no-nk has been a NO-OP on every production run at this tolerance. The campaign was ANK-only whether or not the flag was passed.

attempt_2.change: --nk-switch-tol 1e-4, so NK takes over at 1e-4 and drives to 1e-6
attempt_2.status: ABANDONED on instruction after ~77 min on the first case (alpha 0), against a ~28 min ANK-only norm.

observed_before_abandon.last_lines: Step 0.00-0.01, LinRes 1.000, rho frozen at 5.4642352155e-03 and changing only in the 11th significant figure across iterations 673-675
observed_before_abandon.reading: This is the gci_M freeze signature REPRODUCING ON THE COARSE MESH: NK engages, the Krylov solve achieves no reduction at all (LinRes 1.000), the step collapses, and the residual stops moving.

attempt_2.consequence: The freeze is NOT a mesh-size or memory effect. solve_s8.py attributes it to a lean preconditioner forced by memory at gci_M (12.7 GiB against 12.8 available). gci_C peaks at 6.9 GiB with room to spare and freezes anyway. That hypothesis is therefore not supported -- though the full-preconditioner arm at 1e-4 was never reached, so it is not yet formally refuted either.
attempt_2.data_loss: The run.log carrying this evidence was deleted while cleaning directories that had no result.json. The numbers above were extracted before deletion and are all that survives. Re-running arm C to ~700 iterations would recover it.

still_open: Whether ANK-only and a CONVERGED ANK+NK reach the same forces. Attempt 1 compared ANK against ANK. Attempt 2 never converged. The iterative-convergence verification this study lacks is still missing.
note_for_the_cloud: The documented fallback if ANK-only stalls at gci_F or gci_FF is 'restore ADflow's NK defaults'. On this evidence that fallback may not work, because NK stalls here at 6.9 GiB where memory is not the constraint.
